gaps.wanted: The rack depth the bracket kits span. The guide's Figure 29 and its table name the 19-inch brackets ACC-KIT-T1=, the four-point extension rails and five brackets 4PT-KIT-T2=, and the 23-inch, 24-inch and ETSI brackets RACK-KIT-T1=, and print no range of rack depth, no setback and no part dimension. A kind: kit contract needs a depth or a factory preset, so no kit is written and chassis.kits is left out; the three positions above are named without a number.

A rear drawing of this model. The only held file, NetBox's cisco-c9300-48s.rear.png, is the C9300-24S's file byte for byte, so the rear is carried from cisco/c9300-48p and Figure 10 and is marked estimated.
Whether the front USB Type A storage port is USB 2.0 or 3.0. The guide says only "USB Type A storage port".
The faces of C9300-NM-2Q, C9300-NM-4G, C9300-NM-4M, C9300-NM-2Y and C9300-NM-8X. The guide draws them isometrically and prints no dimension. Left for a later 9300 batch.
The pictograms under the status lamps and beside the mini-USB port. The guide's Figure 8 gives their names and the NetBox elevation draws them at a few pixels each; no legend is drawn.
A flat drawing of the lid, the underside and the sides. The guide's Figure 3 and Figure 10 show them isometrically with a vent on the side and labels on the lid.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

`cpu`, `memory` in a missing `attrs.platform` section; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 6 bays (front 1, rear 5); `physical-context` on port group sfp - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

airflow.note: The Fan Module section: "The airflow direction is from front-to-rear and side-to-rear." One airflow for every build, so there are no airflow configurations.

colour.note: #b7b7b7, the median of the plain face between the left cluster and the first block of cages in the C9300-24S's NetBox front elevation, which is the same picture's face; this model's own elevation reads the same #b7b7b7 in the gap between the cage blocks, the strip under the cages and the left-cluster plate. The merged C9300-48P and its siblings draw #cccccc, read from the pale bar between their jack rows; their own elevation reads #b7b7b7 under the jacks and #d4d4d4 in the gap, so the family's greys differ by the reading, not by a held source. The elevation is a community drawing, not a photograph.

console-over-management.note: The guide's Ethernet Management Port text says the switch is reached "through the 10/100/1000 Ethernet management port or one of the console ports" and the RJ-45 Console Port LED table says the RJ-45 console is disabled while the USB console is active, so the front mini-USB and the rear RJ-45 are one console, and the management port is its own.

front-scale.note: EVERY FRONT POSITION IS READ OFF THIS MODEL'S OWN NETBOX ELEVATION, NOT THE GUIDE'S FIGURE 3, WHICH IS ISOMETRIC. The elevation is 2289 px wide for the 482.6 mm rack face, 4.743 px per mm; it is cropped to the centre 444.5 mm (the body between the ear fold lines), which starts at 90.3 px, and the body's top edge sits 4.1 px under the picture's. Good to about a millimetre. The same measurement on the C9300-48P's picture gave the merged 48P's figures.

left-cluster.note: The beacon button (Figure 3 callout 1, "Beacon LED (UID button)", a lit square), the maker's mark, the Mode button, the status lamps and the USB mini-Type B console port (callout 4) are read off this model's NetBox elevation at the scale of front-scale. THE USB TYPE A STORAGE PORT (callout 5) IS DRAWN AT THE LOWER LEFT, STANDING UPRIGHT UNDER A GRID OF TWELVE VENT SQUARES, not beside the mini-USB as in the 48P's picture, and it is placed there. The guide's Figure 8 names the lamps in two rows, Status, Duplex, Speed and Stack above, then System, Active, XPS and S-PWR, and the Console lamp beside the mini-USB port; the metal prints pictograms and not words, so no legend is drawn and each lamp is named by its id. THE ELEVATION ALSO DRAWS THE PoE PICTOGRAM AT THE END OF THE UPPER ROW; this model has no PoE (Table 18 prints "-" for its available PoE), so no PoE lamp is placed. THE FRONT USB TYPE A PORT'S GENERATION IS NOT STATED: the rear port is "USB3.0-SSD" and the front is only "USB Type A storage port", so it is drawn with the 2.0 tongue.

network-module-bay.note: Figure 3 callout 7, "Uplink network module slots". The bay is read off this model's elevation, which draws a C9300-NM-2Q seated in it: 364.8 to 440.8 mm across and 42.5 mm high. The guide's Table 5 and the Installing a Network Module chapter say the blank C9300-NM-BLANK is fitted "when the switch has no uplink ports (this is required for sufficient air flow)". The blank is the default, so the render shows the blank and not the module the elevation draws. THE NETWORK MODULES THEMSELVES, C9300-NM-2Q, -4G, -4M, -2Y and -8X, ARE NOT MODELLED here and are left for a later 9300 batch; the bay accepts only the blank until they are.

numbering.note: The legends under the strip are the NetBox elevation's: 01 and 12, 13 and 24, 25 and 36, 37 and 48, one pair at the ends of each block. The block-end numbers 12, 24 and 36 are set 1.2 mm right of where the elevation prints them so that the last lamp of the block does not paint over them (lint L21). Port numbering is as printed, and the interface names are not on the metal and are left out.

port-lamps.note: One lamp per port in a strip along the bottom edge, an up triangle for the odd (upper) port and a down triangle for the even, as the elevation draws them. THE ELEVATION DRAWS SEVEN PAIRS OF TRIANGLES ACROSS EACH BLOCK OF SIX COLUMNS, at an 11.7 mm step, which cannot be one lamp per port. The pairs are placed under their own columns, the two triangles 6.4 mm apart as the elevation draws them, and the strip's height is its 40.5 mm below the top. The meaning of each colour is the guide's Table 15 (green link, blinking green activity, amber blocked) and the mode decides which Table 14 reading the lamps show.

ports.note: Table 1 gives 48 SFP ports and the elevation draws 48 cages, in four blocks of six columns, two cages to a column, numbered DOWN each column (odd on the top row, even beneath) as the 48P's blocks are; the elevation prints 01 and 12, 13 and 24, 25 and 36, and 37 and 48 under the four blocks. The cages are 13.5 x 8.5 mm (64 x 41 px) on a 13.96 mm column step (66.2 px) and a 15.7 mm row step, the rows centre 16.0 and 31.7 mm below the top edge, and each block starts 87.5 mm after the last. THE ELEVATION'S COLUMN STEP IS 13.97 AND THE REGISTRY'S FOR std/sfp-ganged IS 14.25, and cells at 13.97 would overlap (lint L13 and L39), so the registry's step is kept, the gutter is 2.0 mm so that each block still starts where the elevation's does, and each block is centred on the artwork: the first and last columns of a block are 0.7 mm off their cages and the middle ones are on them. std/sfp-ganged is the registry's cage for two rows of cages in one bezel slot; each port is typed 1000base-x-sfp by its media and speed.

power.note: Table 1 and Table 18: two power supply slots with a 715 W supply installed by default, PWR-C1-715WAC-P, and "-" for available PoE: no PoE budget is printed and none is written. The guide holds no table of the switch's own draw, and none is written. Table 35 lists the supplies for the series and gives no per-model restriction, so every bay takes all of them.

rack-positions.note: Figures 32 to 35 of the guide draw the front-mounting, mid-mounting, rear-mounting and four-point mounting positions, isometrically, with no dimension. Front-mounting is the first and the guide's Mounting the Switch in a Rack step 1 attaches the brackets for "the front or rear mounting positions"; it is taken as the shipped default. No setback is printed and none is written.

rear-fans.note: Three FAN-T2 modules (the guide: "support three internal hot-swappable 12-V fan modules (FAN-T2=)") at a 63.0 mm step, each 43.9 x 41.1 by Table 48, centred 70.5, 133.5 and 196.5 mm from the left. The StackWise-480 carriers lie between them (92.5 to 111.1 and 156.2 to 174.8 mm) and hold three stacked connectors each, as the elevation draws them, at a 9.3 mm pitch; the guide's Figure 10 points at two ports in all, so each carrier is one port.

rear-left.note: The ground connectors (callout 1) as two ground screws, the USB 3.0 SSD slot (callout 2) under a cover the guide calls the "blank cover on the USB 3.0 SSD slot", the RJ-45 CONSOLE port (callout 4) on the left and the RJ-45 MGMT port (callout 5) on the right, each 14.2 mm from the next, and the lamps for the console and the beacon (callout 3) in the icon row beneath. The jacks' keyways point down.

rear-power.note: The StackPower connectors (callout 7), S-PWR 1 over S-PWR 2, with XPS under the first, at 233.0 mm, and the two supply bays 258.5 and 348.4 mm from the left, each the supplies' 82.55 x 40.1 by the guide's physical table. A 13.5 mm strip of bare chassis closes the right. The guide does not number the supply slots; psu-1 is the left.

rear-scale.note: THE REAR IS CARRIED FROM THE MERGED cisco/c9300-48p, NOT MEASURED ON THIS MODEL. The only held rear file, NetBox's cisco-c9300-48s.rear.png, is the C9300-24S's file byte for byte (COVERAGE.md item 30), so it proves no SKU. It is used as a check: its fans, StackWise carriers, StackPower connectors and two supply bays are where the 48P's rear has them, in Figure 10's order from the left (ground connectors, SSD slot, console and management ports, fan, StackWise, fan, StackWise, fan, StackPower, two supplies). It differs from the 48P's rear in the supply legends (it prints PWR-C1-715WAC-P on both supplies, which is this model's default; the 48P's picture prints PWR-C1-715WAC), in the S-PWR lamp labels, and in drawing the USB 3.0 SSD slot under its blank cover with no port visible. The positions of the merged rear are kept and the SSD slot is kept as a port, as Figure 10's callout 2 names a USB 3.0 SSD port. The supplies are the dark honeycomb faces the components use.

sources.note: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches Hardware Installation Guide, first published 2017-06-20, last modified 2026-05-15, https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/switches/lan/catalyst9300/hardware/install/b_c9300_hig.pdf (sha256 c1db6738...441b). Page numbers are PDF pages with the printed page after them. Table 1 (models, PDF p16, printed 2), Table 18 (default supply, PDF p43 to p44, printed 29 to 30), Table 42 (dimensions, PDF p135, printed 121), Table 43 (weight, PDF p137, printed 123), Table 35 (the supplies), Figures 3, 8 and 10 (the front, the lamps and the rear), the Fan Module section and Table 48. The text layer of those pages was read, not the pictures. COMMUNITY NETBOX DEVICETYPE-LIBRARY ELEVATIONS (cisco-c9300-48s.front.png and cisco-c9300-48s.rear.png, each 2289 x 219) are a second opinion and the only flat drawings held, not Cisco's. No data sheet, no photograph, no 3D model and no stencil is held for the Catalyst 9300.

the-envelope.note: Table 42, the C9300-48S row: 1.73 x 17.5 x 20.7 in (4.4 x 44.5 x 52.6 cm), with the fan modules and the default supplies installed. THE DEPTH IS 20.7 IN, NOT THE 19.2 IN OF THE COPPER MODELS. Width 444.5 (17.5 in; the 44.5 cm agrees). Depth 526.0 (52.6 cm; 20.7 in is 525.8). HEIGHT 44.45, THE RACK UNIT, NOT THE PRINTED 1.73 IN (43.9 mm): the guide prints 1.73 in for every 1RU model and both are nominal, so the unit is carried and the printed height is one millimetre under it. The 17.5 in is the body between the ear fold lines (the NetBox elevation draws ears outside it).

the-licence-suffix.note: C9300-48S-A (Network Advantage) and C9300-48S-E (Network Essentials) differ in software licence only; the guide lists the hardware as C9300-48S throughout. One device, and the suffixed ordering codes are not part numbers of a configuration.

the-rear-figure.note: THE GUIDE'S PDF PAGE 41 REAR FIGURE IS FIGURE 14, THE CATALYST 9300X, AND IS NOT USED. Figure 10 of the guide, "Rear Panel of a Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switch" (PDF page 39), is isometric, one rear for the series. Its callouts name, in order, the ground connectors, the USB 3.0 SSD port, the BEACON LED, the RJ-45 CONSOLE port, the RJ-45 MGMT port, the fan modules, the StackPower connectors, the AC OK and PS OK lamps, the StackWise-480 port connectors and the power supply modules.

vents.note: Three vent strips and the name plate, at the x positions the elevation draws them, which are the same as the C9300-48P's to a millimetre. The first strip is drawn in the elevation as an open crenellated vent and is carried as a vent of the same extent.

weight.note: Table 43, the C9300-48S row: 14.91 lb (6.76 kg) with the fan modules and the default power supplies installed. THE COMMUNITY NETBOX FILE GIVES 7.86 KG (COVERAGE.md item 29); the guide's figure is used.
